content: Braxy is an inflammatory condition that specifically affects the lining of the abomasum, which is the fourth stomach compartment in sheep. This disease is caused by the bacterium Clostridium septicum, also known as Bacillus septicus. The onset of braxy is frequently associated with a dietary shift, particularly when sheep transition from consuming succulent, moist feed to dry or frozen feed. This condition predominantly occurs in young sheep, especially those that have not been immunized with a vaccine targeting Clostridial infections. Meat derived from sheep afflicted with this disease is also referred to as braxy.
